title: Scope firestore.rules text-matching assertions to their collection block and check deny-all ordering in epic_24_stop_the_bleeding_test.dart
rule: TQ-8 (weak assertion vs SR-1..3 rule content)

evidence.quote: // The deny-all rule must come before any collection-specific rules.
final denyPos = rules.indexOf('allow read, write: if false');

'AC2: recordFlutterFatalError is called for Flutter errors',
        () async {

why: 'allows create' and 'enforces completed_at' assert against the whole `rules` string instead of the `_extractBlock(rules, 'completions/{completionId}')` result that the very next test in the same group ('denies update on completions') correctly uses. Nothing stops the points-bound or timestamp-clamp text from being removed from the completions block and coincidentally still matching elsewhere in the file (e.g. another append-only ledger) while this test stays green -- points_ledger and streak_events currently have no such bound at all, so a future accidental swap would go undetected. Separately, the deny-all test's own comment states the rule 'must come before any collection-specific rules' but the assertion only checks `denyPos > -1` (string exists somewhere) -- it never compares denyPos to any collection match's position, so reordering the deny-all rule after a permissive collection rule would not fail this test despite the comment's explicit claim.
recommendation: Change the two unscoped assertions to use `_extractBlock(rules, 'completions/{completionId}')` like the sibling test three lines below; change the deny-all test to assert `denyPos < rules.indexOf('match /completions')` (or the first collection match position) instead of just `> -1`.
acceptance_criteria: The two completions assertions call _extractBlock(rules, 'completions/{completionId}') the same way the 'denies update' test does
The deny-all test fails if the deny-all rule is moved after a collection-specific match block
